classes.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves, turning dark and puckered.
classes.guidance: Prune tree canopy to increase air circulation. Rake and compost or destroy fallen infected leaves to stop spores from overwintering. Avoid overhead watering.
classes.chemical_warning: Fungicide sprays should only be considered during early bud break if confirmed by an agronomist.

classes.symptoms: Small purple spots on leaves expanding into circular lesions with tan centers; mummified black fruit.
classes.guidance: Prune out dead wood, fire blight cankers, and mummified fruit from the orchard. Disinfect pruning shears between cuts with 70% alcohol.
classes.chemical_warning: Never apply fungicides during bloom to protect pollinators.

classes.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or reddish spots on the upper leaf surface.
classes.guidance: Remove nearby red cedar or juniper trees within 1-2 miles if possible. Prune galls from cedar branches in late winter before spores release.
classes.chemical_warning: Preventative sprays only work if applied before visible rust spots form; consult local extension officer.

classes.symptoms: Uniform green coloration, smooth margins, no active lesions or signs of fungal mycelium.
classes.guidance: Maintain routine nutrient feeding, monitor for aphids or mites, and maintain balanced irrigation.
classes.chemical_warning: No treatment required. Avoid unnecessary chemical applications.

classes.symptoms: Vibrant foliage, good shoot vigor, no chlorosis or leaf curling.
classes.guidance: Check soil pH regularly (maintain acidic pH 4.5-5.5). Mulch with pine bark or needle litter.
classes.chemical_warning: No treatment required.

classes.symptoms: White to grayish powdery fungal growth on leaves and young shoots, leaf distortion.
classes.guidance: Prune to improve sunlight penetration and air movement. Avoid excess nitrogen fertilization.
classes.chemical_warning: Neem oil or potassium bicarbonate may be used in early stages with expert verification.

classes.symptoms: Clean foliage, uniform leaf development, no discolored margins.
classes.guidance: Maintain standard orchard hygiene and seasonal pruning.
classes.chemical_warning: No treatment required.

classes.symptoms: Rectangular, tan-to-gray lesions restricted by leaf veins; lesions merge causing leaf blighting.
classes.guidance: Practice crop rotation with non-grass crops for at least 1-2 years. Manage crop residue to reduce fungal survival.
classes.chemical_warning: Fungicide thresholds depend on hybrid resistance and growth stage; request agronomist guidance.

classes.symptoms: Oval to elongate reddish-brown pustules scattered across both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
classes.guidance: Plant resistant hybrid varieties. Rust thrives in cool, humid conditions; maintain good row spacing.
classes.chemical_warning: Treatment rarely economical unless rust appears early on susceptible inbred lines before silking.

classes.symptoms: Long, elliptical cigar-shaped grayish-green lesions that become tan, starting on lower leaves.
classes.guidance: Rotate with legumes or other non-host crops. Deep plow residues after harvest where conservation tillage allows.
classes.chemical_warning: Fungicides are only recommended if lesions threaten the ear leaf before tassel.

classes.symptoms: Broad green leaves, no blights, pustules, or striping.
classes.guidance: Maintain balanced nitrogen-phosphorus-potassium nutrition and weed control.
classes.chemical_warning: No treatment required.

classes.symptoms: Small brown circular spots with black borders on leaves; berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
classes.guidance: Sanitation is vital: destroy all mummified grapes on the vine and ground during winter pruning. Keep canopy open.
classes.chemical_warning: Protective applications must occur between early bloom and 4 weeks post-bloom.

classes.symptoms: Tiger-stripe chlorosis and necrosis between leaf veins; dark spots on grape berries.
classes.guidance: Avoid pruning during damp/rainy weather. Seal pruning wounds with wound protectants. Remove diseased cordons.
classes.chemical_warning: No curative chemical exists. Field management relies entirely on preventative sanitation.

classes.symptoms: Irregular dark reddish-brown lesions with distinct margins on older leaves, premature defoliation.
classes.guidance: Collect and destroy fallen leaf debris after harvest. Ensure adequate vine trellising and airflow.
classes.chemical_warning: Copper-based sprays may be used if severity is confirmed by agronomist.

classes.symptoms: Lush green lobed foliage, clean veins, no spots or powdery coating.
classes.guidance: Continue regular canopy training and shoot positioning.
classes.chemical_warning: No treatment required.

classes.symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy mottle chlorosis across leaf veins, small lopsided bitter fruit with green bottoms.
classes.guidance: Quarantine emergency: notify local agricultural extension immediately! Control Asian citrus psyllid vectors. Use certified disease-free nursery stock.
classes.chemical_warning: No cure once infected; infected trees must be safely removed to protect the remaining grove.

classes.symptoms: Small water-soaked angular spots on leaves, turning purple and dropping out to create a 'shot-hole' look.
classes.guidance: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizers which promote overly lush, tender shoots. Plant windbreaks to reduce sandblast injury.
classes.chemical_warning: Copper sprays during dormancy; strict dosage required to avoid phytotoxicity.

classes.symptoms: Smooth lanceolate leaves, deep green color, free of shot holes or curling.
classes.guidance: Maintain routine pruning and moisture management.
classes.chemical_warning: No treatment required.

classes.symptoms: Small, yellowish-green spots with water-soaked borders turning brown with necrotic centers.
classes.guidance: Use clean, certified disease-free seeds. Never work in wet fields or use overhead sprinkler irrigation.
classes.chemical_warning: Copper bactericides have limited effectiveness if copper-resistant strains exist; agronomist test recommended.

classes.symptoms: Deep green glossy leaves, strong stem structure, no wilting or spotting.
classes.guidance: Ensure regular drip irrigation and consistent calcium to prevent blossom end rot.
classes.chemical_warning: No treatment required.

classes.symptoms: Concentric rings ('target-board' or bullseye pattern) on older lower leaves, surrounded by yellow halos.
classes.guidance: Keep plants vigorous with proper fertility and irrigation. Avoid sprinkler irrigation late in the afternoon. Practice 3-year rotation.
classes.chemical_warning: Screening aid only; confirm severity before purchasing protectant fungicides.

classes.symptoms: Fast-spreading water-soaked pale green to dark brown lesions, white cottony mold under leaves in high humidity.
classes.guidance: HIGH RISK: Spreads rapidly! Destroy infected volunteer plants. Hill potatoes well to protect developing tubers.
classes.chemical_warning: Immediate expert consultation required. Apply protective fungicides only upon agronomist alert.

classes.symptoms: Compound green foliage, erect growth, no necrotic margins.
classes.guidance: Maintain steady hill moisture and monitor for Colorado potato beetle.
classes.chemical_warning: No treatment required.

classes.symptoms: Serrated leaves, bright green surface, clean undersides.
classes.guidance: Prune out spent floricanes after fruiting to improve airflow.
classes.chemical_warning: No treatment required.

classes.symptoms: Trifoliate leaves with vibrant green coloration and no mosaic pattern.
classes.guidance: Maintain routine weed management and scout for pod borers.
classes.chemical_warning: No treatment required.

classes.symptoms: Talcum powder-like white fungal colonies on upper and lower leaf surfaces, causing yellowing and premature drying.
classes.guidance: Plant resistant cultivars. Space rows adequately to maximize sun exposure. Water at soil level.
classes.chemical_warning: Bio-fungicides like potassium silicate or biological bacillus subtilis can be evaluated by an extension officer.

classes.symptoms: Numerous small, dark purple irregular blotches on leaves that enlarge and cause entire leaf to look scorched brown.
classes.guidance: Renovate beds after harvest by mowing old foliage. Clean away dead leaf debris.
classes.chemical_warning: Avoid unnecessary chemical spraying; focus on canopy aeration.

classes.symptoms: Glossy green trifoliate leaves, no purple margins.
classes.guidance: Maintain clean straw mulching to prevent soil splash on fruit and leaves.
classes.chemical_warning: No treatment required.

classes.symptoms: Small, dark greasy spots on leaves often surrounded by a yellow halo, with jagged or irregular edges.
classes.guidance: Do not handle or prune wet plants. Use drip irrigation instead of overhead sprinklers. Rotate tomatoes away from nightshades for 2 years.
classes.chemical_warning: Bactericides have limited efficacy. Agronomist confirmation is advised before spending money.

classes.symptoms: Dark brown concentric rings forming a bullseye pattern on lower leaves; tissue yellowing around the lesions.
classes.guidance: Mulch the soil surface around plants to prevent spores splashing upward. Prune lower suckers 12 inches above ground.
classes.chemical_warning: Screening aid only; confirm with extension officer to distinguish from Septoria leaf spot.

classes.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown-black; white fuzzy mold on leaf undersides in wet weather.
classes.guidance: HIGH EMERGENCY: Can destroy whole fields in days. Bag and remove severely infected plants immediately. Do not compost.
classes.chemical_warning: Urgent expert confirmation needed. Preventive protectants only work before disease spreads.

classes.symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surface, with olive-green to brown velvety patches on underside.
classes.guidance: Common in humid greenhouses or tunnels. Ventilate aggressively to keep relative humidity below 85%.
classes.chemical_warning: Improve air circulation first before attempting chemical interventions.

classes.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with dark brown margins and gray or tan centers with tiny black specks.
classes.guidance: Remove and discard lower diseased leaves as soon as noticed. Stake plants to keep leaves off the damp soil.
classes.chemical_warning: Often confused with early blight; consult agronomist for targeted cultural management.

classes.symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling on leaf surface, fine webbing visible on undersides of leaves.
classes.guidance: Wash leaf undersides with strong water spray. Encourage natural predators (lacewings, predatory mites).
classes.chemical_warning: Broad-spectrum pesticides worsen mite outbreaks by killing predatory bugs; avoid chemical sprays.

classes.symptoms: Small brown spots with subtle concentric rings and light brown centers, lesions expand and coalesce.
classes.guidance: Improve canopy ventilation and practice strict field sanitation. Avoid night-time overhead watering.
classes.chemical_warning: Fungicide options should be confirmed by an agricultural extension specialist.

classes.symptoms: Severe upward cupping of leaves, yellowing of leaf margins, stunted bushy growth, and floral drop.
classes.guidance: Transmitted by whiteflies. Use yellow sticky traps and insect-proof row covers. Immediately pull out and bag infected plants.
classes.chemical_warning: Viral diseases have NO chemical cure. Spraying plants will not cure the virus; focus on vector control.

classes.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green pattern on leaves, fern-like leaf distortion, blistering.
classes.guidance: Transmitted mechanically by hands and tools (and tobacco). Wash hands with soap and water before handling plants. Sterilize pruners.
classes.chemical_warning: NO chemical pesticide can cure plant viruses. Do not waste money on fungicides.

classes.symptoms: Uniform deep green foliage, no spotting, no leaf cupping, healthy growth tips.
classes.guidance: Maintain consistent watering to prevent blossom end rot. Scout weekly for hornworms and aphids.
classes.chemical_warning: No treatment required. Avoid preventative pesticide use.

classes.symptoms: The captured image could not be matched reliably to trained crop diseases.
classes.guidance: Please hold the camera 15-20 cm away from a single leaf, ensure natural daylight, and avoid blurry focus or heavy background clutter.
classes.chemical_warning: DO NOT apply chemicals or pesticides based on an uncertain reading. Always consult an agronomist.
